data.title: Council of Ministers Decision No. (38) of 2026 Amending Certain Provisions of the Executive Regulations of the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Law Issued by Council of Ministers Decision No. (41) of 2019
data.titleClear: Council of Ministers Decision No. (38) of 2026 Amending Certain Provisions of the Executive Regulations of the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Law Issued by Council of Ministers Decision No. (41) of 2019
data.description:
Cabinet / Council of Ministers,

Having reviewed the Constitution,

And Law / Act No. (22) of 2017 on the Regulation of Real Estate Mediation Activities, as amended by Law / Act No. (13) of 2026,

And the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Terrorism Financing Law issued by Law / Act No. (20) of 2019, and the laws amending it,

And Amiri Decision / Resolution No. (29) of 1996 concerning Cabinet / Council of Ministers decisions submitted to the Amir for ratification and issuance,

And Amiri Decision / Resolution No. (28) of 2023 establishing the General Authority for Regulating the Real Estate Sector, as amended by Amiri Decision / Resolution No. (34) of 2026,

And the Executive Regulations of the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Terrorism Financing Law issued by Cabinet / Council of Ministers Decision / Resolution No. (41) of 2019, and the decisions amending them,

And upon the proposal of the Chairman of the National Committee for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT),

Has decided as follows:

files.title: Council of Ministers Decision No. (38) of 2026

almawad.title: Article 1
almawad.description:
The text of Article (59) of the Executive Regulations of the aforementioned Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Terrorism Financing Law shall be replaced with the following text:

Article (59):

«The following supervisory authorities shall be competent to monitor, follow up on, and supervise the compliance of the sectors indicated opposite each of them with the requirements of Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Terrorism Financing:

No.
Supervisory Authority
Sector

1
The Bank
Banks and exchange
Providers of Transfer of Funds or value services
Insurance and reinsurance
Finance and investment companies

2
Qatar Financial Markets Authority
Financial Mediation companies
Qatar Stock Exchange
Qatar Central Securities Depository Company

3
Ministry of Justice
Lawyers
Authorized notaries

4
Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Chartered accountants
Dealers in Precious metals or Gemstones
Trust and company service providers

5
Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority
Entities established in the Centre: financial institutions and Designated Non-Financial Businesses or Professions (DNFBPs).
6
General Authority for Regulating the Real Estate Sector
Real estate brokers
7
Charitable Activities Regulatory Authority
Non-profit organizations
The supervisory authorities include any other entity that legally has the power to regulate or supervise, or is responsible for Financial Institutions Oversight, or for the oversight of non-profit organizations and Designated Non-Financial Businesses or Professions (DNFBPs).».

almawad.title: Article 2
almawad.description: All competent authorities, each within its respective jurisdiction, shall implement this Decision / Resolution. It shall come into force as of 1/1/2027. It shall be published in the Official Gazette.
